downside.story: P10: AI optics capex digestion lands in CY2027-28 (transceiver inventory, 1.6T build slowing; LightCounting itself assumes +50% capex in 2027, src 12) plus an industrial/China leg: wireline -35%, wireless -10%, ADG -4% (continuing resolution), EI -12% (FY24-style downturn; China was 17% of FY25 revenue, src 21), segment margins -5pt (toward the FY25 26-27% mix), P/E -4 turns (ex-SBC basis, ~14.7x / ~16x costed, the FY24 trough rerating), FCF yield +20%, normalised leg -30%.

upside.story: P90: supply loosens and the 1.6T/3.2T cycle runs at the CEO's 20%+ pace: wireline +35%, wireless +6% (6G), ADG +3%, EI +10% (AI semis), margins +2pt on 50%+ incrementals, P/E +4 turns (~22.7x ex-SBC, ~25x costed, near AME), FCF yield -15%, normalised leg +35%.

downside.story: Optics 'bumpy ride' (LightCounting's alternative scenario): the transceiver supply chain overbuilt in 2026-27, Ethernet optics growth falls to ~-4% in 2027 and -18% in 2028 (driver -80 points), CC capture drops 30%, fab equipment growth 20 points lower, ADG 5 points lower; FY27 revenue ~$8.1B, FY28-29 flat to down; margins 4 points lower (~30.5%, FY23 level); P/E 13.5x and FCF yield ~5.2% (trough multiples), normalized leg -40%.

upside.story: Soft landing plus: 1.6T/3.2T and co-packaged optics ramps keep capture nearer the FY26 fit (+0.15), optics growth 15 points above LightCounting, 6G funded development and fab starts add; FY28 revenue ~$11.7B, margins up with incrementals +5 points; P/E 21x (near peer median) and FCF yield 3.45%.

scenario_flags: upside (P90) widened to the multiple-variability floor (19% vol, model 19%)

downside.story: AI networking capex digests in CY2027 (Big-5 capex ~30% below the J.P. Morgan path, i.e. roughly flat on 2026) and test intensity per capex dollar falls (elasticity 0.40): FY27 revenue ~flat at $7.2B, margins back to ~28% as fixed costs built for 20% growth deleverage (FY24 precedent: operating income -39%), fab capex 15% lower, defense budgets held at Senate levels; P/E de-rates to 14.5x and FCF yield widens 35%, as in the 2021-23 -42.6% drawdown.

upside.story: Capex runs 15% above J.P. Morgan (Dell'Oro ~32%/yr path), 1.6T/3.2T production test lifts elasticity to 0.70, FY27 revenue ~$9.1B (+28%, above the 20% base case like FY26 beat its first outlook), margins hold near the Q4 37% CSG exit, P/E 23.5x.

downside.story: 10th percentile: AI-optics test digestion lands in CY2027 (LightCounting Bumpy Ride; 52% of BofA survey respondents expect a hyperscaler capex cut within six months, src 21) on top of AI-SKU supply limits; wireline -35% vs path (FY27 wireline ~1,800, about -9% on FY26), wireless -10% and EI -14% (FY24-type industrial/semis down-leg plus China), segment margins -5 pts back toward FY23-24 levels, P/E -5 turns (~14x ex-SBC, the 2022-24 trough), FCF yield multiple -25%, mid-cycle leg -30%.

upside.story: 90th percentile: supply loosens so the record backlog converts and 1.6T plus 3.2T R&D keep wireline near the market's growth (+30% vs path); wireless +4% on 6G, EI +6%, margins +1.5/+1 pt (CFO's above-40% leverage), P/E +4 turns (~22.9x ex-SBC, near AME), FCF yield multiple +15%.

downside.story: 10th percentile: LightCounting's 'Bumpy Ride' case arrives in 2027-28: hyperscaler 800G/1.6T capacity lands and R&D test budgets pause, so wireline runs 45% below the build (FY28 ~1,950 vs 3,546, about the FY26 level); wireless -8% (an FY24-type RAN/handset pause), EISG -12% (an FY24-type industrial downturn; Kalshi prices a 2027 recession at 20%), segment margins -5pt toward FY25 levels, and the P/E derates 5 turns to ~13.5x as the market prices a cyclical peak (the Oct-2023 trough was 14.6x trailing non-GAAP EPS: 122.05 / 8.33). Like Dec-2021 to Oct-2023 (-42.6% over 22 months, Trefis).

upside.story: 90th percentile: wireline tracks the optics market rather than R&D budgets (LightCounting +76% 2027 holds and 3.2T / co-packaged-optics R&D starts), +28% vs the build; supply eases so the record backlog converts, EISG +6%, margins +2pt, and the P/E re-rates 5 turns to ~23.5x as AI test is treated as structural.

downside.story: P10 (downside case): the mandated China shock (China revenue -50% = 17.5% x 50% = ~8.7% of revenue, 10-K FY25; carried as wireline -10%, wireless -10%, EI -12% inside the deltas) lands on an AI-optics test digestion (LightCounting's October 2026 edition: a 'bumpy-ride' supply-chain correction during 2027-2030 'remains plausible', src 112) so wireline capture falls 30% in total, wireless -12%, EI -15% (FY24-type industrial/auto soft patch), ADG -3%; segment margins -4pt back toward FY24-25; P/E -5.38 turns to the Oct-2023 trough ~15.06x ex-SBC (~16.6x costed), set as a level so any cyclical exit treatment in the base is not counted twice; the -4pt margin cut is earnings, the trough multiple is the market's; FCF yield moved in proportion. Engine $201.47 (round 2026-11-20 set: NVDA Big-4 capex path, filed non-operating lines and the ADG peer fix with Curtiss-Wright on the ex-amortization basis, 2026-11-23).

upside.story: P90 (upside case): supply loosens and the 1.6T/3.2T R&D-plus-production test cycle runs hotter (wireline capture +30%), wireless +5% (6G/NTN), EI +8% (AI semis/PCB), ADG +3%; margins +2/+1.5pt on 60%+ incrementals and Spirent synergies; P/E +4 turns (24.44x ex-SBC); FCF yield in proportion. Engine $525.27 (round 2026-11-20 set: NVDA Big-4 capex path, filed non-operating lines and the ADG peer fix with Curtiss-Wright on the ex-amortization basis, 2026-11-23).
